name: Edmondson’s Psychological Safety Diagnostic
diagnostic: Zero production errors or failures recorded over extended periods; silence in retrospectives; juniors hesitating to question senior architectural assumptions; sudden discovery of systemic defects near release deadlines.

script.label: Vulnerability Normalization
script.text: "Looking through our retro notes, we have not logged a single system failure or mistake in three sprints. In distributed software engineering, silence is not indicative of perfection; it is a leading indicator of risk aversion. As engineering lead, I made an architectural miscalculation on the caching layer last week that elevated latency. I am opening the floor: what system failures or uncertainties are currently remaining unaddressed?"

audit: Do all members answer no to 'a mistake here is held against you'?
Did a junior engineer challenge a senior's pull request in public?
auditFull: Evaluate against Edmondson’s survey: "If you make a mistake on this team, is it held against you?" (Target: 100% negative response rate).
Did junior developers submit RFC questions or dispute a pull request from a senior staff engineer?
foundation: Amy Edmondson’s seminal 1999 study (Administrative Science Quarterly) introduced psychological safety as a team-level climate characterized by interpersonal trust and mutual respect, demonstrating that higher psychological safety correlates with increased error reporting, learning behavior, and unit performance.

origin.title: Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams
